description: STOP WEAK-FOOT USAGE FROM DISABLING A FIRST-TOUCH TRAP VARIANT. WHAT THE STOCK CODE DOES: 0x14404e290 is vtable slot 5 of match::anime::action::CTrapAnimeInfo / CTrapDistAnimeInfo - the 'can this trap variant apply here?' predicate. It is one long AND-chain in which every failure jumps to 0x14404e559 ('xor al,al' = return false). Read directly: (kick class <= 0x15 OR ball speed <= 1.2, at 0x14404e612) AND card 0x4 (0x14404e62f) AND card 0x10 (0x14404e644) AND card 0x15 (0x14404e659) AND, at 0x14404e666, 'mov edx,0x36 / call ATTR_get / cmp eax,3 / jge 0x14404e559' - i.e. the player's Weak-Foot USAGE must be BELOW 3 - AND a distance test against 2.5 (0x14404e67c). So a player who uses his weak foot a lot is locked out of this first-touch variant entirely. WHAT CHANGES: one inline immediate, 0x14404e673 'cmp eax,3' -> 'cmp eax,0x7f'. ATTR_get returns 0..255 through 'movzx eax,al', and weak-foot usage is a small 1..4-style field, so the 'jge' can no longer be taken and the weak-foot term of the chain always passes. Instruction length unchanged; no branch, no pool cell. THE OTHER TERMS ARE UNTOUCHED - the three cards are still required, so this spec only pays off alongside anime-unlock-all.json or a per-player skill-bit write. WHY NOT DO THIS IN DATA: you can lower a player's weak-foot usage to 1 or 2 in the record and open the same gate, but the same field pulls the other way elsewhere - the Feint selector at 0x143fa5b7d wants attr 0x36 >= 1 (below it the selector substitutes animation 0x28) and 0x143fa6d57 wants it <= 2 - and weak-foot usage also drives how often the AI picks the weaker foot at all, which changes error through the weak-foot penalty at 0x143ed787a (3 + 12*(1 - normalised attr 0x27), 3+22 on kick class 4). There is no single value that unlocks everything, and every value you pick has a behavioural cost. Editing this one compare removes the trade-off for this one gate. WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone - the read is of the trapping player's own attribute, no team and no human/CPU branch. EVIDENCE: b-disassembly only. The chain, the compare, the false-return epilogue at 0x14404e559 and the vtable ownership (exe_map: CTrapDistAnimeInfo vf5 starts exactly at 0x14404e290, shared with CTrapAnimeInfo) were all read directly. NOT emulated: I did not drive the predicate with a controlled world, and I did not establish what this variant looks like on screen versus the other trap variants (CFastTrap, CLiftTrap, CSlideTrap, CCancelTrap, CThrough, CStagger). So 'this gate exists and this byte opens it' is solid; 'you will see move X more often' is not. SIDE EFFECTS: making one variant applicable more often shifts the selection distribution among the trap variants - the game will pick this one in situations where it previously fell through to another. If first touches start looking samey, revert this one first. It touches no byte that any other pack touches and has no interaction with the kick-error model. WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH: watch first touches by two-footed players and by players with high weak-foot usage receiving a slow ball in close quarters at short range (the chain also needs ball speed <= 1.2 or a low kick class, and a distance under 2.5). They should now get the same first-touch option their one-footed team-mates already had. Bytes at 0x14404e673 verified identical in the PRISTINE backup and the installed image. A whole-image branch scan reported one apparent 'e9 rel32' at 0x14404dd67 targeting 0x14404e675: that is a byte coincidence inside the real instruction 'sub r9d,0x909' at 0x14404dd65 (the 0xe9 is its ModRM byte), not a branch - verified by aligned disassembly from the function prologue at 0x14404dd40. No real branch lands inside the window. REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/anime-trap-weakfoot-open.json

patches.name: trap variant weak-foot-usage gate: cmp eax,3 -> cmp eax,0x7f (jge to the false-return can no longer be taken)
